reaction: A steward, people who refuse and remember how I answer. That is exactly my kind of promise. Three years sounds long though.
Before I order anyone to cut barley I want to meet someone. Kavak has a little circle beside it; I am guessing that means something is waiting there.
No reply yet. I want to know who lives here before I ask them for anything.
The overseer, with the only glass window. The game calls my impressions guesses, which I like. Rain is two days away, so I will put out the call first and visit after.

input.name: Call the hamlet to cut the landowner’s barley

reaction: I am asking everyone at once. I wonder who refuses.
Ten came, nobody refused. Easier than I feared. Danyal now has a circle, so circles must mean a reply is waiting. A lodging, not a house: a newcomer like me?
I’ll bring my own sickle. A proud little line. Meryem again, a name I knew from another game, but surely a different person; not a recognition. I will visit Danyal properly.
Walking over. I will wait and see what he says.
I am at his lodging but nothing new from him yet. Filled dots appeared on four houses; maybe new replies.

This note is late, after the wait returned at sixty-seven seconds. I am the steward; I need the landowner’s barley cut before rain on 20 July and 384 measures by 15 September. I called the hamlet at twenty-one seconds and everyone came, seventeen people now. Then I chose to visit Danyal because he had a reply circle. I am at his lodging but the visit shows nothing new, and the clock has stayed on 18 July for forty seconds. I cannot tell if the visit is happening or waiting for me. The houses with filled dots tempt me.
I will read the filled-dot houses while the visit runs.
Yusuf wants to reap his own barley first. That is fair; I will not hold to insist. I like that insisting is remembered. Same parenthesised task phrasing as Voice, which feels mechanical.
Same line from Demirci, from an unnamed someone. I suspect Kuyucu and Tepe say it too. I will go back to Danyal, where I actually am.
Come in. And then? I see no way to answer him. Let me look at the actual page.

Oh, there is a whole map: houses as little sketches, the river, dashed lines from the residence, and the rain bar at the top. Much warmer than the text. Danyal says come in; I will let the visit happen.
I am waiting, but for what? It has said 18 July for a minute and a half, and Danyal only says come in. Maybe having his panel open holds time still.

Eight identical lines in a column: After I finish this task (reap our own barley), I will do it. It is fair of them, but it reads like a form, not eight families. The overseer’s advice that some households only listen if you visit is the interesting bit. I will let the afternoon pass and see whether the visit ends.
Walking back already. So the visit was just Come in. I sat by Danyal’s fire for two real minutes and he said two words. I wanted to ask him something, anything. I am not sure what visiting did.
Waiting to reach the residence so I can visit someone who has not answered.
The map and the idea that people remember insisting interest me, but my one visit gave me two words and now I am watching myself walk back on a clock that has not left 18 July.
Still walking.
Home. Yusuf moved to the top saying I cannot do it now, a second time. I will go see a house that never answered at all; the overseer said some only listen if visited.
No reply from Ak. Visiting them.
Oh, the hollow circle is just where I have gone or am going, not a waiting reply. I had that wrong.
I am at the Ak house. Waiting to hear them.
Still no new reply here. Last time Danyal’s words only appeared after I switched panels; maybe the house panel does not refresh.

Maryam is talking at the spring first. That is the first reply that sounds like a person rather than a harvest rule, and I like her for it. The Ak house still has said nothing to me while I sit there.

We weren’t expecting you. That is a good line, and then nothing I can say back. Each visit costs a minute of watching me walk for one sentence, and almost five real minutes later it is still the afternoon of 18 July. I understand the shape: call, read eight identical promises, visit, get one line. I wanted people who answer my answer. I would close the tab here, though it is a gentle stop.
The wish has not passed. I will look at the menu before leaving.
Looking for a stopping choice. I will not type or send anything.
I'm stopping fits. Selecting it locally; nothing typed, nothing submitted.

I am stopping on the afternoon of 18 July, sitting in the Ak house after they said they were not expecting me. Pressing I'm stopping put those words into the note box by itself; I typed nothing and pressed no Submit. I liked the map, Maryam talking at the spring, and being told people remember insisting. But every visit was a walk and one sentence I could not answer, and the replies were mostly the same line eight times. I would not leave it running. I might come back another evening if I wanted a slow valley to watch, and I would be curious to see whether anyone remembers that I never insisted, but I would not return tonight.
